title: Malév 355
summary: Malév Flight 355, an Ilyushin Il-18V with 21 aboard, crashed near Paris-Le Bourget Airport on November 23, 1962 during approach. Weather conditions included heavy fog and stratus cloud with visibility severely reduced. The aircraft initiated a landing on instruments with landing gear extended and engines near full power. During approach, the aircraft stalled while performing a high G-load maneuver and crashed 6.1 kilometers from the airport.
probable_cause: The aircraft stalled during a high G-load maneuver while executing an instrument approach in foggy conditions. The investigation could not determine why the crew performed the high G-load maneuver.

factors.evidence: Very foggy in Paris; pilot noted frequent occurrences of fog and stratus cloud with possibility of light icing; landing was initiated on instruments.
Aircraft stalled while performing a high G-load manoeuvre during approach; the investigation concluded aircraft had stalled while performing this maneuver.
Investigation concluded aircraft had stalled while performing a high G-load manoeuvre during the approach.
Aircraft crashed 6.1 kilometers east-northeast of Le Bourget airport near road from Paris to Soissons.

events.text: Flight 355 departed Budapest at 7:44 GMT with crew and 13 passengers bound for Frankfurt stopover.
In Frankfurt, crew spent two hours at meteorological office for briefing, noting frequent fog, stratus cloud, and light icing possibility.
During approach to Paris with landing gear extended and engines nearly at full power, aircraft stalled while performing high G-load maneuver during approach.
Aircraft crashed 6.1 kilometres east-northeast from airport near road from Paris to Soissons; airplane exploded with high flames visible.

notes: why maneuver was performed remains unexplained
fog and icing conditions contributed to crash
